query:
A group member commented on the Moorland Traverse plan in a way that combined a practical weather observation with a quiet expression of dissatisfaction about the outing format. Who made this comment?

Options:
A. Dmitri
B. Nadia
C. Marcus
D. Bridget
context:
[1] (about=Bridget, core, t2 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) Moorland Traverse works; asks about lunch stop, start time, parking.
[2] (about=Bridget, core, t8 @2025-10-19T15:18:00) Fenwick Edge western approach is better managed and two kilometres shorter; used that version in the old club.
[3] (about=Bridget, core, t10 @2025-10-26T14:47:00) Cairn Ridge confirmed. Asks: who provides group tent pegs and guy ropes? cost-share model for shared gas canisters? contingency plan if weather changes overnight?
[4] (about=Bridget, core, t6 @2025-10-12T14:02:00) Fenwick Edge is a solid route; peat section well-signed now.
[5] (about=Dmitri, core, t20 @2025-11-30T14:32:00) Stoneford continuation is terrain you can only do properly with a night on it. We should do more overnights.
[6] (about=Dmitri, core, t22 @2025-12-07T16:02:00) North ridge system is right choice for three-nighter: two approaches, good escape routes, remoteness. This is what group was working toward. Nadia should lead planning.
[7] (about=Dmitri, core, t18 @2025-11-23T15:47:00) Bothy is fine; simpler than tents in winter; worth doing the full ridge.
[8] (about=Dmitri, core, t2 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) Descent technique: trust friction, don't fight the gravel.
[9] (about=Elena, core, t2 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) The tough ramp is on Ridgeback route, not Moorland Traverse.
[10] (about=Elena, core, t2 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) There's a timed segment on Moorland Traverse (pull up past reservoir); asks who will run it properly.
[11] (about=Elena, core, t20 @2025-11-30T14:32:00) Mapped two timed segments on approach: ascent to col and ridge traverse. Will record times at trailhead.
[12] (about=Elena, core, t12 @2025-11-02T16:02:00) Suggests Ridgeback south spur as optional variant for those wanting steep descent.
[13] (about=Elena, core, t20 @2025-11-30T14:32:00) Noted steep descent in spring plan. Priya has gone from asking about knees on moderate to requesting scree.
[14] (about=Elena, core, t18 @2025-11-23T15:47:00) Descent segment time on Stoneford Ridge west face was 9:02 on wet surface.
[15] (about=Kwame, core, t2 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) Wants to run the timed segment; mentions tough ramp past reservoir (later corrected to Ridgeback route).
[16] (about=Kwame, core, t10 @2025-10-26T14:47:00) Quarry section was incredible; understood the layers thanks to Tomás's explanation.
[17] (about=Kwame, core, t4 @2025-10-05T15:45:00) Enthusiastic about Green Man and the traverse views.
[18] (about=Kwame, core, t21 @2025-12-07T16:00:00) Stoneford bothy trip was the best two days of the year; ridge continuation in dark, col at dawn, mist on day two. Recorded three segments, cried once. No regrets.
[19] (about=Kwame, core, t22 @2025-12-07T16:02:00) Supports Dmitri's suggestion that spring three-nighter should go north; will carry whatever needed.
[20] (about=Kwame, core, t11 @2025-11-02T16:00:00) Cairn Ridge overnight was the best thing the group has ever done; sunrise over plateau at 07:15 was incredible.
[21] (about=Marcus, core, t2 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) Proposes Moorland Traverse for next week, 610m gain, more demanding.
[22] (about=Marcus, core, t10 @2025-10-26T14:47:00) Cairn Ridge planning: will handle technical route; Tomás to take ecology section and mid-route waypoints.
[23] (about=Marcus, said_by=Bridget, profile, t12 @2025-11-02T16:02:00) Route sheet was thorough; made planning straightforward.
[24] (about=Marcus, core, t16 @2025-11-16T15:02:00) Next route: Stoneford Ridge, 640m, good summit. Will plan the technical approach. Tomás can mark the geological point on the waypoints sheet.
[25] (about=Marcus, core, t18 @2025-11-23T15:47:00) Approach to second col is steepest terrain group will have done; 820m total over two days; serious outing.
[26] (about=Marcus, said_by=Saoirse, profile, t12 @2025-11-02T16:02:00) North face was solid; genuinely the kind of route that switches everything off.
[27] (about=GROUP, said_by=Marcus, group-interaction, t2 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) Next week route: Moorland Traverse, 610m gain, start 08:30, parking at eastern layby, lunch at Ridgeback shelter. Confirm by Thursday.
[28] (about=GROUP, said_by=Marcus, group-interaction, t12 @2025-11-02T16:02:00) Next outing: Bracken Tor, 380m, recovery. Optional Ridgeback south spur variant for those wanting steep descent. Confirm by Thursday.
[29] (about=GROUP, said_by=Marcus, group-interaction, t10 @2025-10-26T14:47:00) Cairn Ridge overnight: weekend of November 15-16. Marcus to circulate route sheet by Thursday; confirm by following Thursday.
[30] (about=Nadia, core, t2 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) Moorland Traverse has good weather window; still a day hike.
[31] (about=Nadia, core, t0 @2025-09-21T10:00:00) Confirmed for 28th, 08:30 works, thinks day hike feels short for terrain.
[32] (about=Nadia, said_by=Marcus, profile, t22 @2025-12-07T16:02:00) Marcus says Nadia's planning was excellent; bothy capacity and weather window aligned well.
[33] (about=Nadia, core, t18 @2025-11-23T15:47:00) Wants to do Stoneford Ridge as an overnight using the bothy to access the ridge continuation past the second col.
[34] (about=Nadia, core, t18 @2025-11-23T15:47:00) Stoneford Ridge has a bothy two kilometres past the summit that sleeps ten.
[35] (about=Nadia, core, t22 @2025-12-07T16:02:00) North ridge research starts this week. Preliminary route by end of January. Needs Dmitri's input on safety planning for remote sections.
[36] (about=GROUP, said_by=Nadia, group-insight, t12 @2025-11-02T16:02:00) Cairn Ridge was the best outing; overnight changes everything about how a route lands.
[37] (about=GROUP, said_by=Nadia, group-insight, t18 @2025-11-23T15:47:00) Stoneford Ridge as a day hike clips the top of what it offers; overnight with bothy allows access to ridge continuation past second col.
[38] (about=GROUP, said_by=Nadia, group-interaction, t18 @2025-11-23T15:47:00) Stoneford Ridge overnight bothy trip proposed by Nadia; group shows interest (Kwame, Tomas, Saoirse, Priya, Bridget provisional, Dmitri, Marcus, Elena). Nadia will check availability and post date this week; will send kit list and route details Tuesday.
[39] (about=Priya, core, t18 @2025-11-23T15:47:00) Excited about bothy trip; asks if route has steep sections.
[40] (about=Priya, core, t20 @2025-11-30T14:32:00) Wants at least one spring route with a genuinely steep descent, not just moderately steep. Has gone full convert on challenging descents.
[41] (about=Priya, core, t12 @2025-11-02T16:02:00) Wants a route with steeper descent to keep building confidence.
[42] (about=Priya, core, t16 @2025-11-16T15:02:00) Excited about 640m being the highest day hike. Asks if there's a descent worth doing on it.
[43] (about=Priya, core, t17 @2025-11-23T15:45:00) Stoneford Ridge west face descent was the most fun hike ever; went fast, no hesitation, no ankle paranoia.
[44] (about=Priya, said_by=Elena, profile, t14 @2025-11-09T15:32:00) Priya properly ran that section, not just walking it. Advises trail shoes with more lateral support before winter.
[45] (about=Saoirse, core, t0 @2025-09-21T10:00:00) Confirmed for 28th, asked about descent terrain.
[46] (about=Saoirse, core, t12 @2025-11-02T16:02:00) In for Bracken Tor; asks about descent loose ground.
[47] (about=Saoirse, core, t2 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) Legs are fine; hike was the best part of the week.
[48] (about=Saoirse, core, t10 @2025-10-26T14:47:00) In for November 15. Asks if north face technical enough for crampons or just good boots.
[49] (about=Tomas, core, t2 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) Enthusiastic about Moorland Traverse; mentions limestone pavement near Haver's Edge with three geological periods; offers to plan middle section.
[50] (about=Tomas, core, t10 @2025-10-26T14:47:00) Agrees to take lower ridge section and waypoints through peat for Cairn Ridge; acknowledges Marcus knows north face terrain better.
[51] (about=Tomas, core, t20 @2025-11-30T14:32:00) Can take three from north end for bothy trip. For spring plan, there's a ridge system up north with glacial cirque at head that he's wanted to do for years; overnight only.
[52] (about=Tomas, core, t16 @2025-11-16T15:02:00) Suggests Cairn Ridge again with the lower loop variant, totally different character in winter. Or a new ridge south of the valley with a fantastic contact zone at the summit, used by surveyors back in the day.
[53] (about=Tomas, core, t4 @2025-10-05T15:45:00) Noted Marcus's point about geology detour adding 18 minutes; will stick to path variants with interesting features baked in.
[54] (about=Tomas, core, t16 @2025-11-16T15:02:00) The return path lower section is past the old drovers' lane, which was the main drove route south through the valley. The timed segment would be interesting there, very different surface to the upper spur.
agent_answer: Nadia. She noted the Moorland Traverse had a good weather window, then quietly expressed that it was still a day hike—and that a day hike feels short for the terrain.
